record.original_question: Determine the fixed monthly salary of an employee, measured in dirhams, when the employee worked for a number of days equal to the square root of that salary and received a predetermined amount of money for the month.

evidence.quote: Problem 31 An employee, whose monthly salary is a fixed but unknown number of dirhams, worked during a month for a number of days equal to the square root of the salary and received a predetermined amount of money.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An employee has a fixed but unknown monthly salary of $S$ dirhams, paid for a full month of $30$ days at a constant daily rate of $S/30$ dirhams per day. During a particular month the employee worked only for a number of days equal to $\sqrt{S}$ (so $S$ is assumed to be a positive real number for which this makes sense), and consequently received a known amount of $A$ dirhams for that month, where 
$$A \;=\; \frac{S}{30}\cdot \sqrt{S}.$$
Express the monthly salary $S$ in closed form as a function of the given amount $A$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a classical elementary algebra word problem reducible to the equation $S^{3/2} = 30 A$, with closed-form solution $S = (30A)^{2/3}$. Such problems are routine and considered solved in the standard mathematical literature.

status_evidence.title: Elementary algebra — solving equations with rational exponents
status_evidence.snippet: Equations of the form x^{3/2}=c have the unique positive real solution x=c^{2/3}.
status_evidence.claim: The equation S^{3/2}=30A has the closed-form positive solution S=(30A)^{2/3}, so the problem is solvable in closed form.
